office_does: The State Senator is the 30th District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Claire Wilson, a former Federal Way School Board director, faces first-time Republican candidate Michael Rutland, a retired Air Force senior master sergeant. The race splits on taxes, school policy, and local control.

candidates.summary: Incumbent state senator and former Federal Way School Board director whose record centers on early learning, childcare, and K-12 funding.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and says millionaires should pay their fair share to fund education [S3][S8]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (the 2025 amendments I-1 would undo) and co-sponsored SB 5599 (2023) on youth shelters and protected health care [S9][S11]
Endorsed by WEA-PAC, SEIU 775, and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S15][S16][S17]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and says she will support legislation making millionaires pay their fair share to fund schools.

spending.basis: Runs on landmark childcare and early-learning investments and says education is still critically underfunded.

housing.basis: Cites delivering public resources for affordable housing for low-income families and people leaving homelessness.

safety.basis: Pairs votes for police pay raises and training with funding for drug treatment and recovery.

climate.basis: Describes the clean-energy transition as an opportunity and supports transit to reduce air pollution; no specific carbon-policy position.

experience.basis: Sitting senator and former eight-year school board director, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Co-sponsored SB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care, sponsored the LGBTQ Commission, and campaigns on reproductive rights.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 and sponsored district-selected comprehensive sexuality education, while describing her work as empowering parents' voice.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, retired Air Force senior master sergeant and former Boeing manager, running on cost of living, opposition to new income taxes, and local control.
highlights: Pledges to oppose new income taxes and demand budgeting instead of higher taxes [S1]
Calls for protecting local decision-making and reducing one-size-fits-all state mandates [S3]
Endorsed by the King County Republican Party and former 30th LD Senator Mark Miloscia [S4][S6]

taxes.basis: Repeatedly pledges to oppose new income taxes and calls for budgeting instead of higher taxes.

spending.basis: Calls for responsible budgeting and a government that lives within its means.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and addressing repeat offenses, while also listing prevention and intervention programs.

local-control.basis: Lists protecting local decision-making and reducing one-size-fits-all mandates as a priority.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience, running against a sitting senator.

parental-rights.basis: Says every parent deserves a voice and emphasizes parental involvement and keeping Olympia's 'political agendas' out of schools; no specific notification or opt-out proposal.
